mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which increases consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE shows a sustained decline but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 4.5% indicates tighter monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases while the unemployment rate (UNRATE) also rises, it may indicate labor market inefficiencies, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both PAYEMS increases and UNRATE rises but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, an increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals higher borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in 3 months during a tightening cycle but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: If GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters but SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month while the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4%, it may signal stagflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS > 4%
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS is above 4% but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO increases but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) below 0.1% month-over-month signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If PAYEMS growth is below 0.1% MoM but SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, this hypothesis is rejected.
